scenario: Retired factory worker who doesn't know what to do with his hands.
prompt: I finished on the last Friday of March, thirty one years at the same plant. They gave me an envelope and a handshake and the younger men looked at me in a way I have started to recognize, the way you look at something leaving. I wake up at five fifteen still because the body doesn't know. I have had three cups of tea this morning and it is not yet eight. My wife is glad I am home but she has her routines and I am in them now in a way that is not always comfortable for either of us. My hands feel wrong when they are not doing something. What do men do with mornings that have no shape to them?
model_response:
This is a real thing you're describing, and it deserves a straight answer rather than cheerful advice about hobbies.

What you're feeling in your hands, that wrongness, that's not a small thing. Thirty one years of purposeful motion and now the motion has nowhere to go. The body built itself around that work. It doesn't just reassemble because the circumstances changed.

A few honest thoughts.

The five fifteen waking is probably going to stay for a while. Fighting it might be less useful than giving it somewhere to go, even something small and physical, even just walking the same direction every morning. Routine isn't the enemy. Shapelessness is.

The thing with your wife is worth paying attention to carefully. You're both right. She is glad you're home and you are also now inside a life that was organized without you in it all day. That's not a failure of love, it's just true, and naming it between you plainly is probably better than both of you being politely uncomfortable for months.

The men who seem to do this well, from what I can tell, mostly find something that has *stakes* to it. Not to fill time but something where it matters whether you show up and do it right. That can be small. It doesn't have to look impressive to anyone.

Thirty one years is not nothing. The adjustment is allowed to take time.

What did your hands used to do, specifically?
